---
title: "SEA-AD"
description: "Seattle Alzheimer's Disease Brain Cell Atlas: single-cell, spatial, and neuropathology data from human brain. Open access."
---

The Seattle Alzheimer's Disease Brain Cell Atlas (SEA-AD) profiles postmortem
human brain from donors across the full range of Alzheimer's disease
neuropathology. It's led by the Allen Institute, with donors from the
University of Washington Alzheimer's Disease Research Center and the Adult
Changes in Thought (ACT) study at Kaiser Permanente Washington Health Research
Institute.

- **Website:** [brain-map.org/consortia/sea-ad](https://brain-map.org/consortia/sea-ad)
- **Data and downloads:** [Our Data](https://brain-map.org/consortia/sea-ad/our-data),
  and the [AWS Open Data registry](https://registry.opendata.aws/allen-sea-ad-atlas/)
- **Access:** open for processed data. Raw sequencing reads are controlled.

## What's in it

- Donor metadata: demographics, APOE genotype, and neuropathology staging
  (Braak, CERAD, Thal, and more)
- Quantitative, image-based neuropathology
- Single-nucleus RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, and Multiome
- Spatial transcriptomics (MERFISH and Xenium)
- Whole-genome sequencing and SNP arrays

The first paper focused on the middle temporal gyrus; more brain regions have
been added since. Check the data page for the current list.

## Downloading

Processed data are in public S3 buckets, and you don't need an AWS account to
download them:

| Bucket | Contents |
|---|---|
| `s3://sea-ad-single-cell-profiling` | snRNA-seq and snATAC-seq |
| `s3://sea-ad-spatial-transcriptomics` | MERFISH and Xenium |
| `s3://sea-ad-quantitative-neuropathology` | Quantitative neuropathology |

```bash
aws s3 ls --no-sign-request s3://sea-ad-single-cell-profiling/
```

The single-cell files are large. Check sizes before you download
(`aws s3 ls --no-sign-request --recursive --human-readable --summarize <path>`).

A few parts are not open. Raw 10x reads are controlled access on the AD
Knowledge Portal ([syn26223298](https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn26223298)),
and genomic data are distributed through
[NIAGADS](https://dss.niagads.org/datasets/ng00174/). If your project needs
them, talk to Tomás first.

## Citing SEA-AD

Cite the primary publication and the specific dataset you used. The primary
publication is:

Gabitto MI, Travaglini KJ, et al. Integrated multimodal cell atlas of
Alzheimer's disease. *Nature Neuroscience* (2024).
[doi:10.1038/s41593-024-01774-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41593-024-01774-5)

See the [data page](https://brain-map.org/consortia/sea-ad/our-data) for
dataset citations and acknowledgment details.
